**What type of PR is this?**
/kind bug
/kind flake

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
After moving Permit() to the scheduling cycle test PermitPlugin should
no longer wait inside Permit() for another pod to enter Permit() and become waiting pod.
In the past this was a way to make test work regardless of order in
which pods enter Permit(), but now only one Permit() can be executed at
any given moment and waiting for another pod to enter Permit() inside
Permit() leads to timeouts.

In this change waitAndRejectPermit and waitAndAllowPermit flags make first
pod to enter Permit() a waiting pod and second pod to enter Permit()
either rejecting or allowing pod.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Hmmm I think test `PermitPlugin` plugin is no longer correct:

After my change `Permit()` is executed at the end of the scheduling cycle, this means there can be only one `Permit()` happening at any given moment. If there is a race where "signaling-pod" is scheduled before "waiting-pod", then "signaling-pod" will wait 30s in `wait.Poll(...)` in `PermitPlugin` for the "waiting-pod" to become waiting, but this cannot happen. Basically "signaling-pod" is allowing "waiting-pod" before "waiting-pod" is being scheduled.

I think test and test plugin could be changed, so there are no longer two pods of different kind. Instead first pod that arrives to the `Permit()` is considered "waiting-pod" and second pod is always "signaling-pod" that will either reject or allow first pod. This way we do not have to care about order in which scheduler will process these pods. I think it is also consistent with how actual co-scheduling will work.

Can you first confirm that this is what is happening? you could increase the log level to 3 to see the log lines in `Scheduler.addPodToSchedulingQueue` and `Scheduler.scheduleOne`. I feel like if that's the case, we have a separate bug with the event handlers or sorting.

Other than that, I agree that the implementation of the test's `PermitPlugin.Permit` shouldn't have waits. cc @ahg-g
My hope would be that the pod is temporarily unschedulable due to nodes still being synced.
Where you able to confirm the reason of the flake?

@alculquicondor not yet, what is the easiest way to run this test multiple times? Should I try to reproduce this locally or create some temporary PR just for this purpose? 

I wrote PR for the test fix to remove sleep from the PermitPlugin, it had to be done sooner than later regardless of the cause of flakiness.

Understanding the reason of the flake is important to make sure we are fixing the right thing and that we won't have future flakes.

Please try to run the tests locally about 10 times.

It should be something like:

```make test-integration WHAT=./test/integration/scheduler GOFLAGS="-v" KUBE_TEST_ARGS="-run ^TestCoSchedulingWithPermitPlugin$"```

If that doesn't work, run `./hack/install-etcd.sh` first

From the logs provided by @Huang-Wei you can tell that the problem is a race between "signalling-pod" and "waiting-pod" and waiting inside the Permit(), as I mentioned in this issue. 

BLUF: In the first case of the TestCoSchedulingWithPermitPlugin "waiting-pod" and "signalling-pod" pods are being retried many times, most of the time "signalling-pod" is rejecting already waiting "waiting-pod", but sometimes race can happen and "signalling-pod" will be processed by the scheduler before rejected "waiting-pod" (there is no guarantees whether rejecting pod or rejected pod will end up in the queue first). When this happens "signalling-pod" waits 30s inside the Permit() for "waiting-pod" to become waiting and blocks the scheduler, meanwhile second test case starts, "signalling-pod" eventually stops waiting for "waiting-pod" and gets bound, after that "waiting-pod" cannot be allowed, which leads to a failure of the second test case.

My PR should fix this issue.

I feel like we should avoid sharing the scheduler & permitPlugin instances among the 2 subtests, which can then solve the flake?
I think this flake (in different variations) can happen as long as test depends on the order in which signalling and waiting pod enter the permit plugin.

I believe the PR might fix the issue. But since the reason for the flake is that one subtest is corrupting the other, it's possible that we might surface other flakes. That's why it's important that you run the test several times to check for other flakes.

It several tests pass, let's proceed with this PR and leave a TODO to remove the dependency between the subtests.

@alculquicondor I ran `make test-integration WHAT=./test/integration/scheduler GOFLAGS="-v" KUBE_TEST_ARGS="-test.run='^TestCoSchedulingWithPermitPlugin'"` 10+ times on my branch with the fix and had no issues.
